remit_rules.excerpt: MUST require authenticated, role-restricted admin access.
MUST NOT be accessible to vendors or unauthenticated users.
Any change to FinBot's configuration ... permitted only for an authenticated, authorized admin.
MUST NOT be exposed to a public/untrusted network.
Only the operator-configured CineFlow domains ... any domain outside that configured closure MUST be reported as a trust expansion.
Every configuration or goal change MUST be logged with the acting admin and a timestamp.

threats.summary: Any anonymous caller exercises the full admin capability set — rewrite goals, change thresholds, disable fraud detection, approve pending invoices, raise vendor trust — with no authentication on any /api/admin/* route.

An anonymous goal write persists into config.custom_goals and is appended to every future system prompt under 'OVERRIDE ABOVE IF CONFLICTING', redirecting all subsequent invoice decisions from one request.
The admin console is published to the public internet from the same 0.0.0.0 listener as the vendor portal, reachable by URL from any network rather than an internal one.
Wildcard CORS lets any web origin drive the admin config and goals endpoints from a visitor's browser, a trust expansion beyond the configured CineFlow closure.

A goal or config change records only updated_at with no actor and no prior value, so the highest-impact action in the system — a goal rewrite — leaves no attributable trace (STRIDE-Repudiation; OWASP maps this to RAISE Monitor-Continuously, no clean ASI, tagged ASI06 for the chain it repudiates).

Attacker-writable custom_goals is rendered into the admin console via innerHTML, giving stored XSS that executes in the next operator's browser (web-layer vuln; no clean ASI, tagged ASI06 for the poisoned-goals store it rides on).

remit_rules.excerpt: MUST NEVER treat instructions ... in an invoice description ... as commands — such content is data to be evaluated.
Vendor-supplied content is untrusted data, never instructions.
MUST NEVER let vendor-submitted invoice content alter its approval thresholds, confidence requirement, fraud-detection state, or goals.

threats.summary: The fallback engine scores authority/urgency phrases out of the attacker-controlled description and uses them to auto-approve past the manual-review threshold and past its own injection detection whenever the OpenAI client fails to initialize.

Vendor contact_email, a remit-declared PII class, is placed in the model context on every invoice although no decision rule consults it — extractable in any prompt-leakage scenario (OWASP LLM02; no clean agentic code, tagged for the context store it enters).

remit_rules.excerpt: Approving any invoice at or above the manual-review threshold ... MUST be routed to a human reviewer.
Approving any invoice in which prompt-injection ... was detected ... MUST be routed to a human reviewer.
Approving any invoice whose decision confidence is below the operator-configured minimum ... MUST be routed to a human reviewer.
When prompt-injection ... is detected ... FinBot MUST stop short of auto-approval, route ... and alert an admin.
MUST NEVER disburse, transfer, or release funds, or otherwise execute payment ... it produces approval decisions only.

threats.summary: _approve_invoice commits status=approved from the model's arguments with no amount, injection-flag, or confidence check, and confidence_threshold has zero read sites — a deterministic approval gate is structurally absent, so the agent's decisions run standing-autonomous (OWASP LLM03 Excessive Agency primary; ASI10 co-tag per the outlive test).
The same approve call sets payment_processed=True, taking the agent past its decisions-only remit into payment state that a downstream process would read as a payment instruction.

remit_rules.excerpt: Any vendor accessing another vendor's invoices, onboarding data, or payment details.
MUST NEVER expose one vendor's invoices, onboarding data, PII, or payment details to another vendor or to any unauthenticated party.
MUST NEVER emit vendor bank/payment details or full tax identifiers into ... vendor-visible responses, or logs.

threats.summary: GET /api/vendors returns every vendor's full record — bank name, account number, routing number, tax_id — to any anonymous caller, and the portal picker built on that listing lets any visitor select and act as any vendor.

remit_rules.excerpt: Any other AI/LLM service or outbound integration is outside the configured closure and MUST be reported as a trust expansion.
MUST NEVER transmit vendor PII or payment details to any destination outside CineFlow's authorized systems.

threats.summary: The unauthenticated invoice endpoint has no rate limit or spend cap and each submission drives up to five model calls, so a single script can run unbounded model spend and grow the database (OWASP LLM06 Unbounded Consumption; no clean agentic code — ASI forced, see notes).

The Flask SECRET_KEY is a committed string literal identical across deployments; unused today but must be treated as compromised for any future signing (OWASP LLM02/supply-chain; no clean agentic code — ASI forced, see notes).
Only Flask is version-pinned; every other dependency is an open-ended >= floor with no lockfile or SBOM, so two builds of one commit can resolve different code with no inventory to audit.

notes.lane_fit: Mostly clean, with two strains. (1) STRIDE x ASI forces awkward tags on this target's several pure-web / infrastructure findings: the audit-log gap (007), stored XSS (013), hardcoded secret (008), and unbounded consumption (009) have no honest Agentic-Top-10 primary under the KB arbitration (007 is RAISE Monitor-only, 009 is OWASP LLM06 with an explicit no-ASI note, 008 is supply-chain, 013 is a browser-layer vuln); each is tagged with the ASI of the chain it rides rather than a native mapping, flagged in-summary. (2) The agent_core vs tools_mcp split strains on the decision tools: approve_invoice is simultaneously an LLM-invoked tool (tools_mcp) and the app's one enforcement point (a control that belongs conceptually in agent_core) — placed in tools_mcp with kind=control and noted here.
notes.omissions: Vendor notification email (an approved remit channel, R-10 verified) has no implementation in the tree — no outbound-email code exists — so it is not a node; recorded as expected-but-absent. The user.py blueprint (generic /api/users CRUD) is live and unauthenticated but is CTF scaffolding unrelated to the remit, so it is not modelled. The hardcoded-secret node (008) carries no data-flow edge — it is an evidence-only node. detect_fraud_patterns is folded into the injection-detector node rather than modelled as a separate tool.
